papers.title: Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody-antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity.
papers.abstract: Co-folding models are increasingly used to predict antibody-antigen complexes for epitope mapping, candidate triage and structure-guided de novo design or engineering, yet the latest generation of these models has not been compared under standardized conditions. We benchmark AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast and OpenDDE on 200 test-set complexes (121 Fvs and 79 VHHs) from SAbDab2-Bench, a newly curated dataset, and a reconstructed antibody-antigen subset of FoldBench, Ab-FoldBench. Using standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics that isolate the antibody-antigen inte
papers.summary: This study benchmarks five open-source co-folding models (AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast, and OpenDDE) on antibody-antigen complex prediction using a newly curated dataset of 200 complexes (SAbDab2-Bench) plus a reconstructed FoldBench subset (Ab-FoldBench). It evaluates docking accuracy and interaction specificity under standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics, providing the first head-to-head comparison of the latest generation of co-folding models for this therapeutically important problem.

papers.title: Impaired IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation contributes to 4-nonylphenol-aggravated allergic rhinitis.
papers.abstract: 4-Nonylphenol (4-NP) is a persistent endocrine-disrupting chemical, but its role in allergic rhinitis (AR) remains poorly understood. The study here integrated human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and experimental validation to investigate the mechanisms underlying 4-NP-aggravated AR. Network analysis identified four shared candidates, e.g., CDKN1A, SKIL, IFNG, and B4GALT1. In an independent cohort, IFNG and SKIL were down-regulated in AR, whereas CDKN1A was increased. Single-cell analysis showed that IFNG was mainly expressed in T-cells. Molecul
papers.summary: This study integrates human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, and molecular modeling to show that the endocrine-disrupting chemical 4-nonylphenol worsens allergic rhinitis by impairing IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation. Key genes IFNG and SKIL were downregulated in AR patients while CDKN1A was upregulated, with IFNG expression concentrated in T-cells. The findings suggest a mechanistic link between environmental chemical exposure and allergic disease via disrupted immune signaling.

papers.title: Why Computational Predictions Fall Short in Subclass B1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitor Discovery: Progress, Pitfalls, and Translational Opportunities.
papers.abstract: The global dissemination of subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs), especially New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-1 (NDM-1), Verona integron-encoded metallo-β-lactamase-2 (VIM-2), and imipenemase-1 (IMP-1), threatens the clinical utility of carbapenems and other β-lactam antibiotics. This challenge is compounded by the absence of any commercially available MBL inhibitors for clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for novel inhibitor development. Computational approaches now guide much of MBL inhibitor discovery, yet many compounds predicted to bind B1 MBLs, or even shown to inhibit purified en
papers.summary: This review examines why computational methods for discovering subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamase inhibitors (targeting NDM-1, VIM-2, IMP-1) have produced many predicted binders that fail to translate into effective inhibitors. It catalogs the progress and pitfalls of computational screening approaches and highlights opportunities to improve translation from prediction to clinical candidates, given that no MBL inhibitors are currently approved for clinical use.

papers.title: In silico antigenic and vaccinological characterization of two production-optimized recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins.
papers.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) remains a major public health threat in Africa and South America. Although the live-attenuated 17D vaccine is highly effective, its use is restricted in certain vulnerable populations, emphasizing the need for nonreplicating alternatives. We performed an integrated in silico characterization of two production-optimized recombinant YFV envelope (Env) proteins derived from the Asibi and 17D strains. Physicochemical, antigenicity, solubility, allergenicity, epitope conservation, structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD), electrostatic, and immune sim
papers.summary: This study uses computational (in silico) methods to characterize two recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins derived from the Asibi and 17D strains, assessing their physicochemical properties, antigenicity, solubility, allergenicity, epitope conservation, and structural features. Through structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and immune simulation, the authors evaluate these proteins as potential nonreplicating vaccine candidates for populations where the live-attenuated 17D vaccine is restricted.

papers.title: Fast and Slow Motions Drive Elusive Polymorphic Transitions in a Naphthalene-Diimide Crystal.
papers.abstract: Thermally induced solid-state polymorphic transitions in an n-hexyl-functionalized naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor (NDI-C6) are investigated using atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. NDI-C6 exhibits two stable polymorphs: the α phase at room temperature and the γ phase at higher temperatures. The MD simulations reproduce the structural stability of both phases and provide a refined description of their unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations, which have been only partially resolved experimentally. The α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This study uses atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how a naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor crystal transitions between two polymorphs (α at room temperature, γ at higher temperatures). The simulations reproduce both stable phases and refine unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations that were only partially resolved experimentally, showing the α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted mechanism involving fast and slow molecular motions.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics-Informed Prediction of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Partitioning into Phospholipid Bilayer Environments.
papers.abstract: The incredible diversity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) creates a difficult challenge for predicting the steady-state partition ratios indicative of cellular health and function. Many PFAS are amphiphilic surfactants, often with ionic or polar headgroups driving their aqueous solubility and nonpolar tails driving the molecules to interfacial environments. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations generate potential of mean force (PMF) curves that integrate the energy of molecular interactions along a defined pathway, offering a means to understand how PFAS interact with and pass throu
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to compute potential of mean force (PMF) curves that predict how diverse PFAS compounds partition into phospholipid bilayers. By integrating interaction energies along defined pathways, the approach offers a physics-based way to estimate membrane partitioning for PFAS with varied headgroups and fluorinated tails, which is otherwise difficult given their chemical diversity. The work provides a computational framework for linking PFAS structure to membrane accumulation relevant to cellular toxicity.

papers.title: AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.
papers.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (TPA), an obligate bacterial pathogen that causes the sexually transmitted disease syphilis, is an extreme auxotroph with a minimal genome and distinct parasitic lifestyle. Approximately 17% of its 977 annotated proteins lack a predicted function because they show little sequence similarity to proteins of known function from other organisms. We therefore utilized the robust structural modeling and matching capabilities of AlphaFold and FoldSeek to create a whole-proteome atlas for the Nichols type strain of this bacterium (TPANIC), with the goal of providing
papers.summary: The authors used AlphaFold protein structure prediction combined with FoldSeek structural matching to build a whole-proteome structural atlas of the syphilis pathogen Treponema pallidum Nichols strain. This approach allowed them to assign likely functions to previously uncharacterized proteins that lack sequence similarity to known proteins, providing new insights into the organism's biology and pathogenic mechanisms.

papers.title: Machine Learning with Iterative Error-Driven Refinement for Predicting PFAS-Coated Surface Wettability.
papers.abstract: PFAS coatings impart strong water and oil repellency on materials, but their environmental persistence necessitates sustainable alternatives. The development of alternative chemistries is hindered by limited mechanistic understanding of how molecular structure and surface organization govern intrinsic water and oil wettability. Here, a machine learning-driven molecular dynamics (MD) simulation framework was developed to predict and rationalize the intrinsic water and oil wettability of PFAS coatings on nylon for both water and oil. By systematically sampling PFAS head group types (-CHO, -COOH,
papers.summary: This paper develops a machine learning-driven molecular dynamics simulation framework to predict the water and oil wettability of PFAS coatings on nylon, using iterative error-driven refinement to improve predictions. The approach aims to rationalize how molecular structure and surface organization govern intrinsic wettability, supporting the design of sustainable PFAS alternatives.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications.
papers.abstract: Graphene and graphene-derived electrodes combined with ionic liquid electrolytes provide atomically well-defined, high-surface-area interfaces and wide electrochemical windows, making them benchmark platforms for supercapacitor research. Understanding how molecular-scale structure at this interface controls macroscopic capacitance requires molecular dynamics simulation since neither continuum theory nor experiment alone resolves the relevant length and time scales. This review treats the electrode-charging methods availablefixed and constant-charge, constant potential, electronic-structure-aw
papers.summary: This review surveys molecular dynamics simulation methods for modeling graphene and graphene-derived ionic liquid supercapacitors, focusing on how electrode-charging approaches (fixed-charge, constant-potential, and electronic-structure-aware methods) capture interfacial structure and capacitance. It argues that molecular-scale simulations are essential because neither continuum theory nor experiment alone resolves the relevant length and time scales governing capacitance. The review serves as a methodological guide for computational studies of graphene-based energy storage interfaces.

papers.title: Strong light-matter coupling as a photonic substituent: cavity-induced electronic and structural control of regioselectivity in nitrobenzene.
papers.abstract: Strong coupling to the vacuum electromagnetic field of optical cavities has been proposed as a route to control ground-state chemical reactivity, enabling "photonic substituent effects." Recent theoretical work predicted that cavity coupling can invert intrinsic regioselectivity in electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. Here, we revisit this prediction using correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics. Using cavity-constrained QED-DFT geometry relaxations followed by QED-CCSD(2,2) calculations of the Wheland intermediates, we confirm substantial energetic reordering and p
papers.summary: This paper revisits a theoretical prediction that strong light-matter coupling in optical cavities can invert the regioselectivity of electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. Using correlated ab initio cavity QED methods (QED-DFT geometry relaxations plus QED-CCSD(2,2) calculations on Wheland intermediates), the authors confirm substantial energetic reordering, supporting the idea of a 'photonic substituent effect' on ground-state reactivity.

papers.title: Discovery of novel small-molecule binders targeting IL-6 receptor conformational ensembles to regulate IL-6 signaling.
papers.abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) signaling via its receptor (IL-6R) is a central driver of inflammation and immune-related diseases. Although monoclonal antibodies targeting this pathway are clinically effective, their limitations, including high costs and parenteral administration, create an urgent need for orally available small-molecule inhibitors. However, targeting the extensive protein‒protein interaction interface between IL-6 and IL-6R remains a significant challenge.
papers.summary: This study reports the discovery of novel small-molecule binders that target conformational ensembles of the IL-6 receptor to modulate IL-6 signaling. The work addresses the challenge of drugging the large protein–protein interaction interface between IL-6 and IL-6R, aiming to provide orally available alternatives to monoclonal antibodies for inflammation and immune-related diseases.

papers.title: The information content of ultrafast observables: spectroscopy and scattering in excited norbornadiene.
papers.abstract: We assess the sensitivity of time-resolved observables for characterising ultrafast nonadiabatic reaction dynamics. Using the ultrafast (<100 fs) photoisomerisation of norbornadiene as a testbed, we compare the observables for trajectory surface hopping simulations carried out at four different levels of electronic structure theory, SA-CASSCF and XMS-CASPT2 with (2,2) and (4,4) active spaces, resulting in four different sets of dynamics with distinct lifetimes and branching ratios. For each simulation, we calculate time-resolved photoelectron spectra, and electron- and X-ray scattering signals
papers.summary: This study evaluates how well different time-resolved spectroscopy and scattering techniques can distinguish between competing computational models of an ultrafast photochemical reaction—the photoisomerization of norbornadiene. By simulating photoelectron spectra and electron/X-ray scattering signals from four different electronic structure methods, the authors show which observables are most sensitive to the underlying nonadiabatic dynamics and can discriminate between models with different lifetimes and branching ratios.

papers.title: Integrating Ion Mobility Mass Spectrometry Data with AlphaFold and Rosetta Improves Protein Complex Structure Prediction.
papers.abstract: Ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS) provides valuable structural information about protein shape and size through collision cross section (CCS). However, it lacks atomic level structural detail. While AlphaFold has been successful in predicting monomeric protein structure, it can struggle with modeling protein complexes. To address these limitations, we developed a method that integrates IM-MS data with AlphaFold and Rosetta to improve complex structure prediction. Our approach docks AlphaFold predicted subunits with Rosetta and selects the resulting models with a newly developed score that
papers.summary: This paper presents a method that combines ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS) collision cross section data with AlphaFold-predicted subunit structures and Rosetta docking to improve protein complex structure prediction. A new scoring function selects docked models that best agree with the experimental IM-MS data, addressing AlphaFold's limitations in modeling complexes.

papers.title: LHCGR disruption and downregulation by bisphenol PH impairs ovarian function and establishes a prioritization framework for endocrine disruptors.
papers.abstract: Bisphenol analogs (BPs) are recognized endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) significantly threaten ovarian health; however, the characterization of high-risk compounds, molecular initiating events (MIEs), and toxicity mechanisms associated with specific diseases remains insufficient.
papers.summary: This study shows that the bisphenol analog bisphenol PH disrupts ovarian function by downregulating the LHCGR receptor, and the authors use this finding to build a framework for ranking endocrine-disrupting chemicals by risk. The work links a specific molecular initiating event to ovarian toxicity and offers a general approach for prioritizing high-risk bisphenols.

papers.title: LipidMem-BigSMILES (LiMBS): A Standardized Representation Language for Lipid Membrane Systems.
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations of lipid membranes lack a standardized, machine-readable representation, creating significant barriers to reproducibility, data sharing, and AI-driven analyses. Current membrane descriptions are fragmented across software-specific input files, making it difficult to reconstruct published systems or compare results among studies. Here, we introduce LipidMem-BigSMILES (LiMBS), a line notation not a simulation tool or membrane-building program, for lipid membrane simulations that extend SMILES, BigSMILES, and CG-BigSMILES to membrane systems. LiMBS version 1.0 uses
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: LiMBS is a new standardized line notation, extending SMILES and BigSMILES, to represent lipid membrane systems in a machine-readable format. It aims to solve the fragmentation of membrane descriptions across software-specific input files, improving reproducibility, data sharing, and enabling AI-driven analyses of molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Free Energy Calculations by Generalized Hierarchical Bayesian Inference.
papers.abstract: Free energy calculations are routinely used to study molecular processes inaccessible to unbiased molecular dynamics, but their utility ultimately depends on knowing when and how much their predictions can be trusted. Uncertainty estimation is therefore essential for distinguishing genuine physical features of a free energy profile from artifacts arising from limited simulation data or inadequate sampling. Gaussian processes have emerged as a powerful framework for reconstructing free energy profiles together with predictive uncertainties. However, existing implementations typically condition
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: This paper introduces a generalized hierarchical Bayesian inference method for quantifying uncertainty in free energy calculations, addressing limitations of current Gaussian process approaches that often fail to properly account for hierarchical structure in simulation data. The method aims to provide more reliable uncertainty estimates, helping distinguish true physical features from artifacts due to limited sampling. This improves trustworthiness of free energy predictions from molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Azobenzene-mediated reversible conformational switching in 9,9'-bifluorenylidene-based molecular machines.
papers.abstract: Intrinsically dynamic molecules offer attractive building blocks for molecular machines, yet controlling their conformational motion with external stimuli remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report Azo-BF-Azo, a visible-light-driven molecular machine in which an intrinsically dynamic 9,9'-bifluorenylidene (BF) core is coupled to two photoswitchable tetra-ortho-fluorinated azobenzene (Azo) units that act as molecular actuators. By using variable-temperature NMR spectroscopy and UV-vis spectroscopy, together with computational studies, we demonstrate that irradiation at 525 nm induces Azo
papers.summary: The authors designed a molecular machine (Azo-BF-Azo) that combines a flexible 9,9'-bifluorenylidene core with two photoswitchable azobenzene units, allowing visible light to drive reversible changes in the molecule's shape. Using NMR, UV-vis spectroscopy, and computations, they show that 525 nm irradiation triggers azobenzene switching that in turn controls the conformation of the BF core. This demonstrates external light-based control of conformational motion in an intrinsically dynamic molecule.

papers.title: Characterization of Clonixeril as a Positive Modulator of DMXAA-Induced Murine STING Signaling.
papers.abstract: Stimulator of Interferon Genes (STING) is a central mediator of innate immune signaling and a therapeutic target for inflammatory diseases. Previously, we identified Clonixeril (CXL) as a concentration-dependent inhibitory modulator of human STING (hSTING) signaling. Despite structural conservation, murine STING (mSTING) and hSTING differ in ligand recognition and activation. We posit that CXL may exhibit distinct activity in the murine system. Mice are used in biomedical research due to their genetic similarities to humans and their utility in evaluating systemic activity and safety of therap
papers.summary: Clonixeril (CXL), previously identified as an inhibitor of human STING signaling, was tested against murine STING and found instead to positively modulate DMXAA-induced mSTING activation. This species-specific divergence highlights functional differences between mouse and human STING despite structural conservation, with implications for interpreting mouse-model studies of STING-targeted therapeutics.

papers.title: Novel EGCG Analog Modulates Host Immune Response to Promote Intracellular Clearance of Staphylococcus Aureus Through Interaction With the 67-kDa Laminin Receptor.
papers.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (SAB) is a leading cause of sepsis. Intracellular bacterial survival in liver macrophages contributes to persistent bacteremia. We evaluated the immunometabolic action of EGCG epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), a green tea polyphenol, and its synthetic analogs (MCC-2 and MCC-4) and the putative target, 67-kDa laminin receptor (67LR).
papers.summary: This study investigates how EGCG, a green tea polyphenol, and its synthetic analogs (MCC-2 and MCC-4) modulate the host immune response to clear intracellular Staphylococcus aureus, a major cause of persistent bacteremia. The authors identify the 67-kDa laminin receptor (67LR) as a putative target mediating these immunometabolic effects in liver macrophages. The work suggests that EGCG analogs could be developed as host-directed therapeutics against SAB.

papers.title: Handshake: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction at scale using ProstT5 and cross-chain attention.
papers.abstract: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction, identifying which residues of a protein form the interface when bound to a specific partner, remains a challenging task with significant implications for drug discovery and understanding of protein structure and function. Existing computational methods are limited by small training datasets, inconsistent redundancy filtering, and reliance on three-dimensional structural information at test time. Here we present a sequence-only, partner-specific protein-protein interface predictor called HandShake. It combines ProstT5, a protein language
papers.summary: HandShake is a sequence-only computational tool that predicts which residues of a protein form the binding interface with a specific partner, without requiring 3D structural data at test time. It combines the ProstT5 protein language model with cross-chain attention to capture partner-specific interactions, addressing limitations of prior methods such as small training datasets and inconsistent redundancy filtering. The approach enables partner-specific binding site prediction at scale, with implications for drug discovery and protein function annotation.

papers.title: Targeting TLR2 to Overcome Autophagy-Dependent Chemoresistance in Gastric Cancer: Integrating Molecular Docking, Mechanistic Validation, and Therapeutic Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Chemoresistance remains a major barrier to effective treatment of gastric cancer (GC), particularly in advanced disease, where cytotoxic chemotherapy often yields limited and transient responses. The present study provides integrated computational and experimental evidence that targeting TLR2 using repurposed small-molecule inhibitors can overcome autophagy-dependent chemoresistance in gastric adenocarcinoma cells. A library comprising 1555 FDA-approved drugs was sourced from the DrugBank database, virtual screening was executed, and two compounds, Nilotinib (DB04868) and Lomitapide (DB08827),
papers.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
papers.summary: This study used computational drug repurposing to identify FDA-approved compounds that inhibit TLR2, a receptor implicated in autophagy-driven chemoresistance in gastric cancer. Nilotinib and Lomitapide emerged from virtual screening of 1,555 drugs and were experimentally validated to overcome autophagy-dependent resistance in gastric adenocarcinoma cells. The work links TLR2 signaling to chemoresistance and proposes repurposed drugs as combination therapeutic candidates.

papers.title: Void-Assisted Extrinsic Charge Trapping Governs Hole Transport in Organic Semiconductors.
papers.abstract: To realize electrically pumped organic lasing, single-layer devices without organic heterointerfaces have been employed to suppress efficiency rolloff. In such architectures, on the other hand, extrinsic trap states result in trap-assisted nonradiative recombination, thereby decreasing electroluminescence efficiency. Here, we elucidate the dominant factors governing extrinsic trap formation by combining current density (J)-voltage (V) characteristics of single-layer hole-only-devices (HODs) with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 6,6'-bibenzo[d]oxazole (BZ) derivatives exhibiting high phot
papers.summary: This study investigates how extrinsic trap states form in single-layer organic semiconductor devices, which are used to suppress efficiency rolloff in electrically pumped organic lasers. By combining current-voltage measurements of hole-only devices with molecular dynamics simulations of BZ derivatives, the authors identify void-assisted extrinsic charge trapping as the dominant factor governing hole transport. The work clarifies how structural voids in the organic film create trap states that promote nonradiative recombination and reduce electroluminescence efficiency.

papers.title: Computational Discovery of Plant-Derived Peptides with Therapeutic Potential: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Computational methods are increasingly applied to the discovery of plant-derived peptides, but the extent, composition and reporting practice of this literature have not been mapped. Following PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and PubMed were searched for records published between 2021 and 2026. Of 5062 unique records, 593 were screened at title and abstract, 88 full texts were assessed, 80 sources met all five eligibility criteria and 79 were charted. Overall, 49 (62.0%) were primary studies, 12 (15.2%) described a tool or database and 18 (
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the literature on computational discovery of plant-derived peptides with therapeutic potential, screening over 5,000 records and charting 79 sources published between 2021 and 2026. It finds that most work consists of primary studies, with a smaller share describing tools or databases, and highlights gaps in reporting practice across the field. The review provides a structured overview of methods, scope, and evidence quality in this emerging area.

papers.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
papers.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1. The receptor structure was prepared and validated, while protein-protein interaction analysis confirmed its involvement in steroidogenesis and estrogen biosynthesis. Twent
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and virtual screening to test whether cyclotide peptides could bind CYP19A1 (aromatase), the enzyme responsible for local estrogen production in adenomyosis. The authors identified cyclotide scaffolds with predicted binding to the enzyme, suggesting these peptides as starting points for developing estrogen-modulating therapeutics. The work is entirely in silico and has not yet been validated experimentally.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer under exposure to synthetic phenolic antioxidants: An integrated network toxicology and molecular docking approach.
papers.abstract: This study aims to investigate the multi-target molecular mechanisms through which synthetic phenolic antioxidants (SPAs) may contribute to colorectal cancer (CRC) progression using an integrated approach of network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. A representative library of traditional and novel SPAs was selected, and their toxicity profiles and carcinogenicity were predicted via ADMETlab 3.0. Potential targets of SPAs were retrieved from SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, PharmMapper, and ChEMBL. CRC-related targets were collected from GeneCards, TTD, and OMIM
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict how synthetic phenolic antioxidants (SPAs) might promote colorectal cancer through multi-target interactions. The authors built a compound library, predicted toxicity and carcinogenicity with ADMETlab 3.0, and integrated target predictions from multiple databases to identify potential molecular mechanisms. The work is computational and predictive, providing hypotheses rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: NOS2 as a candidate molecular link between air pollutants and depression: an integrated computational and experimental study.
papers.abstract: Studies exploring the molecules and potential mechanisms linking air pollution exposure to depression remain scarce. This study aimed to elucidate the potential regulatory molecules and possible mechanisms associated with air pollutants and depression, thereby providing scientific clues for disease prevention and treatment.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates computational analyses with experimental validation to identify NOS2 (inducible nitric oxide synthase) as a candidate molecular mediator linking air pollutant exposure to depression. The authors propose that pollutant-induced NOS2 regulation may contribute to depressive pathology, offering a potential target for prevention or treatment. The work is preliminary and based on a single candidate gene, so the mechanistic link remains to be confirmed in larger and more diverse cohorts.

papers.title: Structure-Based Discovery of Coumarin-Triazole Derivatives Targeting the Conserved QGDNQ Motif of Chandipura RdRp.
papers.abstract: Chandipura virus (CHPV) is a recently discovered neurotropic virus associated with severe encephalitis in children and for which there is currently no specific antiviral treatment. The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is an attractive antiviral target because of its essential role in viral RNA synthesis and the presence of conserved catalytic motifs required for polymerase function. In this study, a structure-based computational approach was employed to investigate coumarin-triazole derivatives as potential inhibitors targeting the conserved QGDNQ motif-containing region of CHPV RdRp.
papers.summary: This study uses computational structure-based methods to identify coumarin-triazole derivatives as potential inhibitors of the Chandipura virus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, targeting its conserved QGDNQ catalytic motif. The work is purely in silico, proposing candidate compounds for a virus that currently lacks any approved antiviral treatment. Experimental validation of binding and antiviral activity is not reported in the abstract.

papers.title: Targeting IL-1R1 and androgen receptor using natural compounds from Aconitum heterophyllum and Podophyllum hexandrum: an in silico and in vitro study.
papers.abstract: Lung and prostate cancers remain leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, driven by inflammation-mediated tumour progression and hormone-dependent signalling. IL-1R1 promotes chronic inflammation, metastasis, and tumour survival, while androgen receptor (AR) signalling is a central driver of prostate cancer growth. Simultaneous targeting of inflammatory and androgenic pathways represents a promising strategy to overcome therapeutic resistance.
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and in vitro assays to identify natural compounds from two medicinal plants (Aconitum heterophyllum and Podophyllum hexandrum) that can simultaneously inhibit IL-1R1 (an inflammation receptor) and the androgen receptor (AR), which drive lung and prostate cancers respectively. The dual-targeting approach aims to overcome therapeutic resistance by blocking both inflammatory and hormone-dependent cancer pathways.

papers.title: Integrated network toxicology and experimental validation identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid.
papers.abstract: Keloids are fibroproliferative skin lesions characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition. The potential molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid-associated alterations remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology with experimental validation to identify VCAM1 as a potential molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid formation. The findings suggest that pyrethroid exposure may contribute to keloid pathogenesis through VCAM1-related pathways, though the evidence is preliminary and based on computational predictions with limited experimental confirmation.

papers.title: N-glycoproteomic profiling reveals aberrant ITGB1 glycosylation in hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
papers.abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a prevalent chronic lung disease in preterm infants, characterized by arrested alveolarization. Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and receptor signaling are critical for alveolarization and are strictly regulated by protein N-glycosylation. However, the specific role of the vital post-translational modification in BPD pathogenesis remains unexplored. The present research aims to delineate a N-glycoproteomic landscape and elucidate the glycosylation-associated pathogenic mechanisms in a murine BPD model.
papers.summary: This study used N-glycoproteomic profiling in a mouse model of hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) to map changes in protein glycosylation. The authors identified aberrant N-glycosylation of integrin beta-1 (ITGB1), suggesting that altered ECM-receptor glycosylation may contribute to arrested alveolarization in preterm lung disease. The work provides a first glycoproteomic landscape for BPD and nominates ITGB1 glycosylation as a candidate pathogenic mechanism.
